sophia: What does your manager think of the new dashboard?
you: She like the real-time view a lot.
reply: Nice! She likes it. Ready for your status update?
tip: she likes: com he, she e it, o verbo ganha -s.

sophia: Quick status for the global team?
you: We is on track for go-live next Friday.
reply: Perfect. “We're on track” sounds very natural.
tip: on track = no prazo, dentro do planejado.

sophia: Why did the margin go up this quarter?
you: Our margin went up because cost came down.
tip: went up / came down: o par mais útil para falar de números.

sophia: Tell me about a project you're proud of.
you: I leaded a team of five through a tough rollout.
reply: Strong start! Now tell me the result.
tip: led é o passado de lead. Verbo forte para entrevista.

sophia: Excuse me, do you have this in a medium?
you: Let me check if we have it in medium.
tip: Let me check compra tempo com gentileza.

sophia: I'm not feeling well. My arm hurts.
you: Can you show me where it hurt?
reply: Well done. And remember the “h” sound.
tip: hurts, com o “h” soprado: um som que costuma confundir brasileiros.
